old: “Of the calamities of the fort and the treasury, that of the treasury is the graver,” says Pishuna.

why: reviewer (minor): garīyaḥ is rendered 'more serious' in chunk 1 of this chapter and in p08/ch03; and the supplied predicate should be bracketed as chunk 1 does ('(is more serious)'), since the Sanskrit line has no predicate.

old: The fort can be won over by instigation by means of the enemies' treasury.
new: The fort can be won over by secret instigation by means of the enemies' treasury.
why: reviewer (minor): Glossary fixes upajāpa = secret instigation (chunk 1 of this chapter also uses 'secret instigation').

old: liable to be won over by instigation
new: liable to be won over by secret instigation
why: reviewer (minor): Same glossary rendering.

old: n. acc. sg.
new: m. acc. sg.
why: reviewer (minor): durga is masculine in this chapter (35 durgaḥ, labelled m. nom. sg.); labelling durgam here neuter is inconsistent.

old: For it is seen that those who possess forts are not exterminated — so ends the view.
new: For it is seen that those who possess forts are not exterminated.
why: reviewer (error): Unsupported addition: the closing iti is not a phrase 'so ends the view'; chunk 1 renders a closing iti by the quotation mark alone, and Kautilya's reply carries no quotation marks in the e-text.

old: क्योंकि दुर्गवालों का उच्छेद न होना देखा जाता है — इस प्रकार यह मत है।

old: iti closes Kautilya's reply (8.1.37-40).

old: “Of the calamities of the treasury and the army, that of the army is the graver,” says Kaunapadanta.
new: “Of the calamities of the treasury and the army, that of the army (is more serious),” says Kaunapadanta.
why: reviewer (minor): Same as 33: fixed rendering 'more serious', supplied predicate in brackets.

old: Kaunapadanta's view continues to 8.1.45. pratigraha = 'receiving, keeping hold of'; sva-daṇḍa-pratigraha could also mean 'the winning over of one's own troops'.
new: Kaunapadanta's view continues to 8.1.45. pratigraha = 'receiving, keeping hold of'; sva-daṇḍa-pratigraha could also mean 'the winning over of one's own troops'. pratigraha is also the technical term for the army's reserve force (Book 10), so 'keeping a reserve of one's own army' is another possible reading.
why: reviewer (minor): pratigraha is also the technical term for the reserve of an army (Book 10); 'keeping a reserve of one's own army' is a live alternative that the note should record. Translation left as drafted; medium confidence is right.

old: inf. √piṇḍ (caus.)
new: inf. piṇḍ- (cl. 10, piṇḍayati)
why: reviewer (minor): piṇḍayati is a class-10/denominative stem, not a causative of a primary root.

old: And in the absence of a treasury the army can be held together by means of forest produce, land, or the seizing of the enemy's land for oneself; and by one who possesses an army a treasury can be gathered.
new: And in the absence of a treasury the army can be held together by means of raw materials, land, or the seizing of the enemy's land for oneself; and by one who possesses an army a treasury can be gathered.

old: with forest produce
new: with raw materials
why: reviewer (minor): Same glossary rendering.

old: kupya = forest produce / raw materials, kept literal. 'can be gathered' in the last clause is carried over from śakyaḥ ... piṇḍayitum.
new: kupya = raw materials (forest produce), per glossary. 'can be gathered' in the last clause is carried over from śakyaḥ ... piṇḍayitum.

old: Because it sets all things in motion, the calamity of the treasury is the graver — so ends the view.
new: Because it sets all things in motion, the calamity of the treasury is the more serious.
why: reviewer (error): garīyaḥ fixed rendering is 'more serious'; '— so ends the view' is an unsupported addition for iti (see 40).

old: सब द्रव्यों का प्रयोजक होने के कारण कोश का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है — इस प्रकार यह मत है।
new: सब द्रव्यों का प्रयोजक होने के कारण कोश का व्यसन अधिक गम्भीर है।
why: reviewer (error): Same addition in Hindi.

old: “Of the calamities of the army and the ally, that of the ally is the graver,” says Vatavyadhi.
new: “Of the calamities of the army and the ally, that of the ally (is more serious),” says Vatavyadhi.

old: For one who possesses an army the ally remains in the condition of an ally, or even the enemy comes to be in the condition of an ally.
new: For one who possesses an army the ally remains in the condition of an ally, or the enemy comes to be in the condition of an ally.

old: दण्डवान् का मित्र मित्र-भाव में बना रहता है, अथवा शत्रु भी मित्र-भाव में आ जाता है।
new: दण्डवान् का मित्र मित्र-भाव में बना रहता है, अथवा शत्रु मित्र-भाव में आ जाता है।
why: reviewer (minor): 'भी' is not in the Sanskrit.

old: m. gen. du. (dvandva)
new: n. gen. du. (dvandva)
why: reviewer (minor): An itaretara dvandva takes the gender of its last member; mitra is neuter, so the compound is neuter (cf. 33, 53 labelled n.).

old: anabhyantara = 'not internal', i.e. an outsider; the sense is that the ally is of no avail in these cases.
new: anabhyantara = 'not internal', i.e. an outsider; the sense is that the ally is of no avail in these cases. anabhyantara could also be a third dvandva member: 'in a revolt of the enemy, the forest chief or one not of the interior (an outsider)'.
why: reviewer (minor): The draft reads anabhyantara as an adjective on kopa; it can equally be a third dvandva member ('an enemy, a forest chief or an outsider'), given the Arthashastra's pairing abhyantara-/bāhya-kopa. Translation left as drafted; record the alternative.

old: When calamities occur simultaneously and when the enemy grows, the ally stands by only in connection with its own advantage.
new: When calamities occur simultaneously and when the enemy grows, the ally stands firm where there is a connection with gain.
why: reviewer (error): 'only' and 'its own' are unsupported additions (the note admits 'only' is interpretive); artha-yuktau is simply 'where there is a connection with gain'.

old: व्यसनों के एक साथ आने पर और शत्रु की वृद्धि होने पर मित्र अपने अर्थ के सम्बन्ध के अनुसार ही टिकता है।

old: in connection with its own advantage
